items.text: Foundation Office
A door at the far end of the hallway shuts, blocking out the muffled sounds of conversation.
As the four-hundred-year-old tale comes to an end, its listener scratches her head.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: So, after that, you went back to Zhu County and became a constable?
Chéng shakes his head.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: For some reasons, I failed to become a constable that year.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I gave the iron shuttle to Lì Huìfēng, and he only smiled.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But when I met you, it seemed you'd already been a constable for quite some time. Arresting people, shouting orders—you were actually rather skilled at it!

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I was lucky. Three years later, another constable position opened up. I succeeded in filling it.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hm?

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: So, this story of yours has something to do with this box?
A finely crafted wooden box rests on the wooden table in the middle of the room. The lid has been removed and placed beside it.
Inside is a bill of exchange, listing the Hú family in the capital, and an amount of ten thousand taels of silver.
It also reads: "Bestowed upon Doctor Xiù, presented to Chéng Héguāng."

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Interesting. The East Asia branch just told me they had an old artifact in their warehouse, one that's been lying around for centuries.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I heard it had once belonged to the Hú family, with specific instructions to pass it on to a man named Chéng Héguāng, possessor of a rather unique arcane skill.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But where would we find someone to honor it? Surely they've all long forgotten about this thing by now.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I've never heard of anything like this before. So much has happened since then. I never returned to that Riverside Village.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah! With all this money, were you still in Huanzhou, you'd be living a life of leisure with not a care in the world.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But now times have changed. The Hú family is long gone.
And the once valuable bill of exchange is just another useless scrap of paper.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But why would she gift you all this?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I don't know. I suppose now I never will.
Paper Heron suddenly smiles, as if recalling something. She paces back and forth twice before finally walking to the door.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: This elder ... Perhaps all she wanted was for you to live an unworried life.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Either way, I've done what was asked of me. I'll be on my way. Thank you for the story, Héguāng.
The door closes, and Chéng is left standing alone in the room.
Side Room, Clinic

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Are you leaving?
Chéng nods as he finishes packing up his bundle.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Matters are settled here. I need to head back right away.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Here, take this medicine. It'll help with her cough.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I'm surprised you're letting me go.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I thought, at the very least, you'd resent me for what happened with your father.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: He made his decision. And he took responsibility for his actions.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Sometimes I think you're much more alike to us bandits than your vaunted officials.
Chéng puts the medicine in his bag and stops for a moment.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Do not misunderstand me. If you return to banditry, I will show you no mercy.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: It doesn't matter what anyone's intentions were. Things happened as they did, and everyone has paid the price.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Your price is to be a doctor, and mine is to be a constable. It is for the best.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: You had no hand in all this. It's not your fault. You are not your father.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I know, but that changes little.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: You probably think me a rambler by now, but ...

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Why not stay in the village, hm? Live the life of a tiger-slaying hero? Why go back and put up with all that scrutiny?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: The offer is tempting. Slaying that tiger was indeed exhilarating.
But what do titles and glory matter to a hero that has more than himself to think of?
One who has a beautiful white house in Zhu County, where his mother still lives. One who is the son of Chéng. It is that hero's duty to protect that little white house.
And how can he leave before the walls are repainted white?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: In the end, I'll always be the son of a bandit.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Constable or bandit, they're only words.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: They're more than just words. They're a gateway to the martial arts, to handfuls of silver, and to life-saving medicine.

"Just as the art enjoyed by the elite and the common folk differs, so does their etiquette. Outside the home, one listens to teachers and superiors; inside the home, one follows the manners of one's mother."
The people of the county hold the works of sages and scholars as unquestionable truth.
"One must hold compassion and kindness for others, even when in crisis. One must carry integrity, justice, and honesty, even when in poverty."
But none of them hail the brute who saved the village from a tiger.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: True righteousness can only be delivered through true righteous acts.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: When I become a constable, I will be fair and do right by the people. This I swear.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Were I in charge of the militia here, I never would have let that tiger wreak havoc for so long, and I wouldn't have let any people die.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Nor would I have let those refugees starve. None of this would have happened.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: You'll need to be a great general if you're to stop it from ever happening again.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Once I become a constable, I will rise through the ranks: militia captain, regional commander ... Becoming a general will be within my grasp!

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: If only all it took were grand words, eh? But that's not how the world works.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: She shakes her head.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: But then again, if you can truly live a life of wealth and glory, I suppose that's not such a bad compromise.
She smiles, a hint of melancholy in the curve of her mouth.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: Officials have always had beautiful homes. Perhaps your parents hoped as much for you.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: But should things go awry someday, you know where to find me.

items.speaker: Doctor Xiu
items.text: I'll help you.
Zhu County looks just as it did before. The streets are filled with pretty houses, one on top of the other, and all topped with black tiles.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Constable and bandit are only words.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I've been away for so long. I wonder how things are at home.
Chéng passes beneath three Paifang, and the familiar sight of his home comes into view.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: That year, I had planned to sell the house and set aside some money. Those who came to look all praised it, calling the courtyard splendid and the house magnificent.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: A good house keeps its wealth hidden. You'd never know whether it was filled with gold and jewels or rolls of the finest silks.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: *cough* They walked in full of envy but left sighing and grumbling.

items.speaker: Mother
items.text: Because there was nothing to be found in our house.
Because a tomb is a house for the dead.
And a home can be the same for the living.
This ancient house has played host to countless masters, and now it adds one more to its history.
A long white banner flutters in the wind, scattering the red Mei blossoms on the ground.
Another gust of wind blows into the room, sweeping away the thin, pale bill of exchange.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Seeking victory in the wrong place only invites further misfortune.
The bill floats out the window, soaring higher and further like a bird in flight.
Until it goes beyond the range of his arcane skill, becoming a barely visible white dot in the distance.
Paper Heron pokes her head around the door.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Oops. My memory's terrible, you know! There's something else I forgot to mention.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I bumped into some folk from the East Asia branch of the Vigiles Bureau. They're looking to recruit you.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You know of them, right? Their job is like that of a constable's: catching thieves, writing reports, and that sort of thing.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Anyway, I'm just passing along their message. So, what do you think?
Chéng looks at the empty box. A barely perceptible smile crosses his face.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Let's talk about it later.
He remembers an old house. A white house.
A house that welcomes life into the world. A house that bids farewell to those who pass.
A house that has laid to rest Father, Mother, and friends.
A house with clearly defined edges, square and stern in its form.
A house consumed by fierce flames.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: I could never find what I'm seeking in that home.

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: So I burned it down and left.
